drivingQuestion: In the mishna's case, what do the other brothers say?
outcomeNote: Provisionally resolved: they say 'he is not our brother' (challenged in the next unit).

segments.he: ״זֶה אָחִי״ – אֵינוֹ נֶאֱמָן. וְאִידַּךְ מַאי קָאָמְרִי? אִי קָאָמְרִי ״אֲחוּנָא הוּא״, אַמַּאי יִטּוֹל עִמּוֹ בְּחֶלְקוֹ וְתוּ לָא? אֶלָּא דְּקָא אָמְרִי ״לָאו אָחִינוּ הוּא״?
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that one who says: «This is my brother,» is «not deemed credible» with regard to his other brothers’ share of their father’s inheritance. Rather, the man in question receives a portion only from the portion of the one who testified concerning him. The Gemara clarifies: «And what do the other» brothers «say? If they say: He is our brother, why» does the man in question «take» a portion of the inheritance only «with» the one who testified, «from his portion, and nothing more?» If the other brothers admit that he is their brother, they should give him a share of their portions as well. «Rather, they are saying: He is not our brother.»
